rows.title: TRUNK-6795: Populate obs reference ranges in a save handler so they survive validation.disable
rows.excerpt:
_Requested by **dkayiwa** · [Slack thread](https://openmrs.slack.com/archives/C021QUDSD5K/p1788308814384069)_

## Description of what I changed

**Before:** `ObsValidator` did two unrelated jobs at once. As well as reporting values that fall outside a concept's absolute range, it was the only thing in core that worked out an observation's reference range and interpretation and wrote them onto the `Obs`. Validators are only ever reached through `ValidateUtil.validate`, which returns immediately when the `validation.disable` global property is switched on. An implementation running with that property therefore saved every observation with no reference range and no interpretation at all — no error, no warning, just missing data that cannot be reconstructed afterwards, because the range criteria are evaluated against the patient's state at the time of the observation. The validator also overwrote any reference range a caller had already set on the observation.

**After:** deriving the reference range and the interpretation is a save-time concern, handled by a new `ObsSaveHandler`. Save handlers are dispatched by `RequiredDataAdvice` before, and independently of, validation, so an observation now gets its reference range whether validation is on or off. A reference range supplied by the caller is left alone rather than being replaced with a freshly derived one. `ObsValidator` keeps `validateAbsoluteRanges` and every `error.value.outOfRange.*` rejection; its remaining job is validation, and nothing else.

**How:** `setObsReferenceRange(Obs, ConceptReferenceRange)`, `setObsReferenceRange(Obs)` and `setObsInterpretation(Obs)` moved out of `ObsValidator` into `ObsSaveHandler`, which is registered as `@Handler(supports = Obs.class, order = 50)` and implements `SaveHandler`. The handler reproduces the guards that used to gate the population inside the validator: it skips voided observations, obs groups, non-numeric datatypes, numeric observations with no value, and observations with a null concept. Group members are covered because `RequiredDataAdvice.recursivelyHandle` already walks the `Obs.groupMembers` collection — the field carries neither `@Independent` nor `@DisableHandlers` — so the handler does not recurse itself. `ObsValidator` still looks the `ConceptReferenceRange` up for itself; reusing the one the handler derived is not safe, because `Obs.get

rows.title: TRUNK-6512: Introduce ConceptReferenceRangeContext API
rows.excerpt:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **dkayiwa** · [Slack thread](https://openmrs.slack.com/archives/C021QUDSD5K/p1788308814384069)_

## Description of what I changed

This is a backport of TRUNK-6512 to the `2.7.x` maintenance branch. It is ported from the current state of `2.8.x` rather than cherry-picked from the original 2.7.x commit, because that commit (`f127132c`) was written against the old Velocity-based criteria utility, which TRUNK-6610 has since replaced with SpEL on this branch.

**Before:** resolving a concept reference range on 2.7.x means going through an `Obs`. `ConceptService.getConceptReferenceRange(Person, Concept)` fabricates a throwaway `new Obs(person, concept, null, null)` and hands it to `new ObsValidator().getReferenceRange(obs)`, and the whole selection algorithm — evaluating each range's criteria, falling back to the `ConceptNumeric`'s own bounds, and merging multiple matches into the strictest range — lives inside the validator. A caller that only has a person and a concept, or that wants ranges evaluated as of some date other than today (retrospective data entry, for instance), has no way to say so: the criteria are always evaluated against a synthetic Obs with a null `obsDatetime`.

**After:** there is a first-class `ConceptReferenceRangeContext` that carries the person, the concept, an optional evaluation date, and — when it was built from one — the originating `Obs` and `Encounter`. `ConceptService.getConceptReferenceRange(ConceptReferenceRangeContext)` resolves a range from that context, and the selection algorithm now lives in `ConceptServiceImpl` where the rest of the concept logic is, instead of in a validator. Criteria expressions can use `$context` alongside the existing `$patient`, `$obs`, `$encounter`, `$date`, and `$fn`, and `$date` now reflects the context's date rather than always coming from an Obs.

## How

- New `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/ConceptReferenceRangeContext.java`, with constructors for `(Person, Concept, Date)`, `(Obs)`, and `(Encounter, Concept)`.
- `ConceptService`/`ConceptServiceImpl` gain the `ConceptReferenceRangeContext` overload; `ConceptReferenceRangeUtility` gains `evaluateCriteria(String, ConceptReferenceRangeContext)`.
- The existing `evaluateCriteria(String, Obs)` and `getConceptReferenceRange(Person, Concept)` signatures are kept and now delegate to the context-based versions,

rows.title: TRUNK-6768: Remove unused BOM entries and ban SNAPSHOT dependencies in release builds
rows.excerpt:
## Description of what I changed

This PR audits the BOM against actual module usage, removes unused managed entries, and adds a release-build check that fails on SNAPSHOT dependencies.

Changes:

### 1. BOM Audit (`bom/pom.xml`, `web/pom.xml`)

Audited every managed dependency in `bom/pom.xml` against what `api`, `web`, `webapp`, and `liquibase` actually declare or resolve (via `mvn dependency:tree`).

**Removed (confirmed unused anywhere in the module tree):**
- `org.openmrs.liquibase.ext:type-converter` — confirmed unused via dependency:tree across all modules

**Kept, with explanatory comments** (per the ticket's "deliberately provided with a comment" criterion):
- `jaxen` — required transitively by the `liquibase` module for XML changelog XPath support; not declared by `api`/`web`/`webapp`
- `netty-bom` — pins the Netty version pulled in transitively via the AWS SDK S3 client
- `sonar-jacoco-listeners` — used as a listener dependency for the jacoco-maven-plugin / Sonar coverage integration in the root pom.xml, not a direct project dependency

### 2. Release-build check for SNAPSHOT dependencies (`pom.xml`)

Added a `release` Maven profile using the built-in `banDynamicVersions` Enforcer rule, bound to the `validate` phase, which fails the build if any resolved dependency has a SNAPSHOT version, a version range, or a LATEST/RELEASE placeholder.

Tested:
- `mvn validate -pl api` → passes (normal dev builds unaffected)
- `mvn validate -Prelease -pl api` → fails with a precise message naming the offending SNAPSHOT dependency

### 3. What's NOT included, and why

The ticket also asks for milestone (`-M`), alpha, beta, and RC qualifiers to be banned in release builds. I was unable to implement this with `bannedDependencies` (the rule the ticket suggests) or any other built-in Enforcer rule:

- `banDynamicVersions` only covers SNAPSHOT, version ranges, and LATEST/RELEASE — milestone/alpha/beta/RC versions are not "dynamic" by Maven's definition and are explicitly out of scope for this rule.
- `bannedDependencies`' wildcard support only replaces a *whole* segment (groupId, artifactId, or version) or accepts a real Maven version range. It does not support partial substring matching within the version field (e.g. `*-M*`). rows.title: maven(deps): bump org.owasp.encoder:encoder from 1.4.1 to 1.5.0
rows.excerpt:
Bumps [org.owasp.encoder:encoder](https://github.com/OWASP/owasp-java-encoder) from 1.4.1 to 1.5.0.
Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

OWASP Java Encoder 1.5.0

Version 1.5.0 is available from Maven Central. All nine binary/source/Javadoc JARs, four POMs, and their thirteen signatures were downloaded from Central and verified against the retained signed release files. There is no encoder-esapi:1.5.0 release.

Security and correctness

  • Fixes encoded fragments completing outer HTML or XML parser delimiters across trusted-text boundaries in JavaScript HTML/block, CDATA, and XML-comment contexts. Versions through 1.4.1 are affected. See GHSA-g8p6-7r8f-qrpv.
  • Fixes EncodedWriter close/finalization behavior, exception handling, and overflow-safe array-slice validation.
  • Adds JSON encoding APIs and matching JSP/Jakarta tags and EL functions, plus XML 1.1 bindings.

Compatibility and migration

Public Java APIs remain binary and source compatible with 1.4.1 for the three supported libraries. Java 8 remains the minimum runtime; packaged consumers passed on Java 8, 11, 17, 21, and 25.

The security fixes deliberately change some encoded output:

  • JavaScript HTML/block modes emit additional hexadecimal escapes while preserving the string value. Review byte snapshots, cache keys, signatures, and output-size budgets.
  • CDATA preserves parsed text but can expand to 13 output characters per input character and can change parser event boundaries.
  • XML-comment hyphens become ~ under the documented lossy policy.

The optional ESAPI adapter is retired. Version 1.4.1 is its final published release and is unsupported; migrate to direct Java Encoder APIs. Mixing the 1.4.1 adapter with the 1.5 core is not a supported migration.

See the migration notes,
